title: seed_draft_with_token's raw UPDATE is redundant after the W1 mint-at-save fix
detail: The round-2 upsert mints the token on INSERT (upsert_application_draft.sql: 'INSERT INTO application_draft (vacancy_id, email, fields, continue_token) SELECT $1::uuid, lower($2), $3::jsonb, $4'), so on a fresh row passing `token` as arg 4 yields identical state; the follow-up UPDATE is leftover from round 1's 3-arg upsert.
recommended_fix: Drop the pog.query UPDATE and pass the desired `token` as the upsert's 4th argument in seed_draft_with_token.

title: Four new public draft routes have no router-level pin; the /erase sibling has exactly that test
evidence:
http.Put, ["apply", code, "draft"] ->
      draft_handler.handle_save_draft(req, ctx.config, code)
    http.Post, ["apply", code, "draft"] ->
      draft_handler.handle_save_draft(req, ctx.config, code)
    http.Post, ["apply", code, "continue-link"] ->
      draft_handler.handle_continue_link(req, ctx.config, code)
detail: Every chunk-3 test calls handlers directly (e.g. draft_integration_test.gleam's save_draft helper: 'draft_handler.handle_save_draft(req, test_server_config(db), code)') or pins pure functions with literal path lists; no test drives these arms via router.handle_request, unlike the /erase precedent (gdpr_integration_test.gleam:2069: '403 would mean CSRF middleware intercepted — exactly the regression this test pins'). A dropped arm — or GET resume swallowed by the SPA catch-all (router.gleam:864 'http.Get, _ -> serve_spa_shell') — would pass the suite while 200-ing the landlord shell in production.
recommended_fix: Add one router.handle_request smoke test per new arm (mirroring the /erase CSRF router test) asserting the draft handler runs rather than the catch-all/404.
